issues.sym: The van slips between gears, revs without speeding up, shifts late or harshly, or stops moving in Drive or Reverse.
issues.why: The 41TE four-speed automatic in these vans is the most-reported failure, usually between about 85,000 and 130,000 miles. Old or wrong fluid makes it worse; it needs Chrysler ATF+3/ATF+4 type fluid.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and make sure only the correct Chrysler fluid is used. If it slips or will not move, get a transmission shop diagnosis before driving it further.

issues.sym: The van suddenly holds one gear, feels sluggish, and revs high on the highway. Restarting may clear it for a while.
issues.why: When the transmission computer sees a fault from a sensor, solenoid or worn clutch, it locks in a fail-safe gear to protect itself. Chrysler issued bulletins to make the computer less sensitive to brief glitches.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes read before clearing anything. Sometimes a sensor, wiring or software fix is enough; sometimes it is the first sign of internal wear.

issues.sym: The speedometer, gauges and dash lights stop working off and on, sometimes coming back after a bump or a tap on the dash.
issues.why: Cracked solder joints inside the instrument cluster and loose wiring connections are the usual causes as the cluster ages.
issues.next: Have the cluster tested. A cluster repair or rebuilt unit usually fixes it. Do not drive without a working speedometer and fuel gauge.

issues.sym: Clunks or creaks from the front over bumps, rust visible around the tops of the front struts under the hood, or alignment that will not stay set.
issues.why: The front strut towers on 1996-2000 Chrysler minivans are known to rust through. Chrysler made repair kits to reinforce them.
issues.next: Have the strut towers inspected for rust, especially in salt-belt states. Badly rusted towers are a safety issue and need repair before the strut tears loose.

issues.sym: Power steering fluid drips under the front, the pump whines, or the steering gets heavy, especially at low speed.
issues.why: The steel power steering lines rust over time and start leaking. A worn pump can also groan or lose assist when hot.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level. Replace leaking lines before the pump runs dry and fails.

issues.t: Brief loss of power steering in turns
issues.sym: The steering suddenly gets heavy for a moment while turning, usually at low speed with the A/C or defroster running.
issues.why: Chrysler issued a bulletin for a momentary loss of power assist on these vans when the A/C load and steering load combine at idle.
issues.next: Mention the symptom and the bulletin to a shop. Check the power steering fluid level and belt condition first.

issues.sym: Coolant loss with no visible leak, white exhaust smoke, overheating, or oil that looks milky.
issues.why: Head gasket leaks happen on these engines, often after overheating. Chrysler introduced an updated multi-layer steel head gasket through service bulletins.
issues.next: Stop driving if the engine overheats. Have a cooling system pressure test and a combustion leak test done.

issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, puddles under the front, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: Owners of these vans often report leaking radiators, water pumps and hoses as they age.
issues.next: Keep the coolant topped up and have the leak found with a pressure test before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Rear heater lines rust and leak
issues.sym: Coolant leaking under the middle of the van, a sweet smell, or the coolant level dropping on vans with rear heat.
issues.why: Vans with rear heat or A/C run long steel coolant pipes under the body that rust out over time.
issues.next: Have the lines checked when the coolant level drops. Replacing just the rusted pipes is often an option instead of replacing the whole system.

issues.sym: A groan or moan from the engine bay with the A/C on, a burning rubber smell, a squealing or broken drive belt, or warm air from the vents.
issues.why: Chrysler issued bulletins for compressor lock-up at low mileage, compressor moaning and cracked A/C lines near the compressor.
issues.next: Turn the A/C off if it is groaning or the belt squeals. A seized compressor can shred the belt that also drives the alternator and water pump.

issues.sym: Wet carpet on the front passenger side, especially after rain or with the A/C running.
issues.why: Chrysler bulletins describe water leaking from the heater and A/C housing onto the passenger floor.
issues.next: Have the HVAC housing drain and seals checked. Dry the carpet to stop mold and musty smells.

issues.t: Stalls or hesitates after a hot restart
issues.sym: Rough idle, hesitation or stalling right after restarting a warm engine, or trouble starting it hot.
issues.why: Chrysler issued engine computer bulletins for hot-restart stalling, sags and rough idle.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a dealer or shop about the engine computer update for these symptoms.

issues.sym: A light ticking or tapping from the top of the engine at idle.
issues.why: Chrysler issued a bulletin for valve train ticking at idle on these engines.
issues.next: Check the oil level first. If the oil is fine and the tick does not get worse, it is usually not urgent, but have it diagnosed.

issues.t: Oil leaks from valve covers and front seal
issues.sym: Oil spots under the van, a burning oil smell after driving, or oily residue on the engine.
issues.why: Valve cover gaskets and the front crankshaft seal harden and leak with age and high mileage.
issues.next: Watch the oil level. Fix leaks that drip onto the exhaust, since that can cause smoke or a fire risk.

issues.t: Front-end clunks from ball joints and tie rods
issues.sym: Clunks or pops over bumps or while turning, uneven tire wear, or loose-feeling steering.
issues.why: Ball joints, tie rod ends and sway bar links wear on these heavy vans. Chrysler also issued bulletins for front-end popping and suspension groans.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Worn ball joints and tie rods should be replaced and the van aligned.

issues.sym: The speedometer drops to zero or jumps around, and the transmission may shift oddly.
issues.why: The vehicle speed sensor fails, which also confuses the transmission computer.
issues.next: Have the speed sensor checked and replaced; it is a fairly simple repair.

issues.sym: A window will not go up or down, moves slowly, or makes grinding noises.
issues.why: The window motors, regulators and switches wear out.
issues.next: Test the switch first; if it is fine, the motor or regulator needs replacing.

issues.t: Clock spring can disable the driver airbag (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag light comes on, and the horn or steering wheel buttons may stop working.
issues.why: The clock spring, a coiled ribbon wire behind the steering wheel, can be wound wrong or wear through, cutting the driver airbag circuit. Recalls 02V-293 and 04V-480 replace it.
issues.next: Do not ignore an airbag light. Have a dealer check both recalls by VIN.

issues.sym: A raw fuel smell under the hood or fuel wetness around the injectors.
issues.why: The O-ring seals on the fuel rail break down and can leak fuel near hot engine parts. Recall 00V-268 covers vans with the 3.3L and 3.8L V6.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, do not drive the van. Have a dealer check the recall.

issues.t: Cylinder head oil plug can leak and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Oil smell or smoke from the engine bay.
issues.why: A plug in the oil passage of the 2.4L engine's cylinder head can push out and spray oil on hot parts. Recall 96V-006 adds a retaining bracket.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the bracket was installed. Any smoke from under the hood needs immediate attention.

issues.t: Fuel system leak and vapor recalls
issues.sym: A fuel smell near the tank or filler, or fuel seeping near the fuel pump.
issues.why: Three 1996 recalls cover fuel leaks at the fuel pump mounting (99V-216), static buildup in the ungrounded filler tube (96V-002) and a rollover valve that could let fuel reach the vapor canister (95V-236).
issues.next: Have a dealer check all three recalls by VIN. Do not ignore a fuel smell.

issues.t: Rear bench seat bolts can break (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning sign. A rattle or loose rear bench seat can be a clue.
issues.why: Some rear bench seat bolts were brittle and could break, letting the seat come loose in a crash. Recall 95V-225 replaces them.
issues.next: Have the recall checked by VIN and do not carry passengers on a loose rear seat.

issues.sym: The built-in child seat harness is hard to release, routed wrong, or the seat feels loose.
issues.why: Recalls covered broken child seat mounting bolts (96V-136), a harness latch that sticks when dirty (98V-185) and harness webbing routed wrong (97V-231).
issues.next: Have a dealer check all child seat recalls before using the built-in seats.

issues.t: Loose trim can jam a rear seat belt (recall)
issues.sym: A rear outer seat belt will not pull out or retract.
issues.why: Interior trim can fall into the rear outboard seat belt retractor and jam it. Recall 02V-076 covers it.
issues.next: Do not seat anyone in a position with a jammed belt. Have the recall done.

issues.t: Tires and steel wheels can lose air suddenly (recall)
issues.sym: A tire goes flat suddenly or keeps losing air.
issues.why: Some factory tires on steel wheels could lose air without warning (97V-200), and some steel wheels were scored during tire mounting (97V-070).
issues.next: Most original tires are long gone, but if your van still has its original steel wheels, have them checked under the recall.
